[PAGE 1]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, 0raz10 Terrano. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
I work hard for my money ... 
 
When I pay for a product, it should be 100% mine, to do as I want. 
 
Having even a portion of that product taken away, is equivalent to taking part of my 
hard earned money. 
 
Are the manufacturers planning to cut the prices of their products to reflect what will be 
no longer mine ??? 
 
It's as simple as that !!!

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, A. Chaudhuri. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

We run a 40acre vegetable farm. I have avoided new technology just for the reason 
that you have to pay 150$ an hour for a service tech to come to the farm and tell you 
what's wrong. We live out in the middle of nowhere and there billing starts when they 
leave their shop, so right off the bat it would be a $300 bill just to diagnose. Most of 
these people are not any more trained at mechanics than i am the only difference is 
they can work on the proprietary software.  This country was built on self reliance and 
that's what i stand for. When i pay 60k for a tractor i should be able to diagnose and fix 
it, plain and simple.Ú

I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Adam Hasselwander. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

But instead of doing what they're elected to do, they take the side of the folks that paid

sectors and maximize profits. That they do this at the expense of the majority of 
[PAGE 47]
Americans has not escaped the notice of Americans, or the authorities, but the 
authorities choose to do nothing. So how long is it going to be before Americans get 
entirely fed up with it all and start to take action themselves? We saw what happened 
after the 2008 economic crash, with the backlash of protests against the financial 
industry all around the US. That was fairly small scale and put down relatively easily. 
We saw it on a larger scale with the Arab spring in so many Arab countries, where 
people protested against the harsh regimes in place, usually US-backed regimes. 
 
People are not animals to be herded and controlled. They're to be treated with respect, 
which means respecting their right to own and modify anything they please, having 
legally paid for it, and therefore legally owning it. But of course, Capitol Hill has set itself 
outside of the laws that govern the US majority, so the folks there don't care. And most 
are so wealthy they can buy their freedom to do what they want anyway, so again, they 
don't care. 
 
But it's a certainty that if things keep going like this, despite the dumbing down of the 
US population, there are more and more people that see what's happening. It's doubtful 
they'll stand for it longer term, whether on a personal level or as a whole. So it's time 
the US administration started doing what it's consistently failed to do for decades, 
which is to act for the people - remember that statement - government of the people, for 
the people and by the people? Well that's the standard by which the US administration 
needs to be judged, and it has failed the people for many, many years, especially as 
those doing the governing are far from being "of the people"! This US administration 
can still choose to uphold the correct principles, and a small way of doing that, 
demonstrably, would be to reject the interference from agenda-ridden corporations and 
similar, and allow us all the freedom to do what we want with our own devices. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Andrew Akers. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
I currently drive a little '82 truck. All the inner workings are mechanical, and I've spent 
many Saturdays out in the driveway, tinkering, repairing, modifying. I have guides 
produced by people who have taken apart the car and put it together again, I have tools 
specifically adapted to the job. However, if I bought a new car, I wouldn't have access 
to an increasingly important area of the engine, the electronics. I wouldn't have any 
guides, because no one could take it apart. I wouldn't have any tools, because no one 
would know boe to make them. Americans should have an unfettered right to repair 
and modify their own vehicles. These days, though, many manufacturers now put 
digital locks on the embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, 
computer-controlled vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's 
lawful owner, from tampering with those locks for any purpose. I want to be able to 
tinker, without worrying about lawyers. I want to be able to modify, without having to 
resort to breaking the law. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Andrew Jaques. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
My father is a farmer, and one of the more important lessons I've learned from him is 
that older= more reliable. Farmers- at least small scale ones, operate on small margins, 
this is why most farmers are jacks of all trades, you just cant afford to pay for an 
electrician, plumber, repairman, engine specialist, etc etc when you are constantly 
needing those services on your farm. John deere, and many others like them, have 
been trying and succeeding at creating a market that used to be filled by the farmers 
themselves. By creating digital locks they ensure a steady supply of cash as farmers 
must contact a company repairman to fix the very tractors they own. This sort of 
protectionist thinking is extremely short sighted. First you need to consider that the 
prices of older versions (the ones without fancy computers) is actually rising, and that 
sales of newer models are falling. Then factor in the lack of investment in newer 
technology since the demand/funding is slowly but steadily drying up. Finally look at 
how this is affecting the farmers themselves- a problem that they used to be able to fix 
by tinkering around for a few hours now takes days just waiting from someone from a 
company that doesn't even have an office in the same county to arrive, then diagnose 
the problem, then wait even longer to order parts and wait for them to arrive. In the 
short term this is making fields lie fallow for days at a time when harvesting season 
lasts only two weeks, costing the farmer even more money than the repair itself, and in 
the long term it is destroying the basics of a strong economic market for newer 
machines. The argument for removing DMCA restrictions should be more than strong 
enough looking at just the economic impact. That's without even considering the idea of 
what ownership really is if your restricted from fixing your machine yourself for the sole 
reason that some company wants to milk you for even more money than they got for 
the cost of hundreds of thousands dollar machines. And here my dad had always 
taught me that we were only supposed to milk dairy cows! 
[PAGE 129]
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles.  We shouldn't be left to the 
mercy of the manufacturer or service providers to provide affordable or timely services 
to equipment that's essential to my livelihood. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Blake. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Since when was it ever illegal to repair a car? Are you kidding me? This is how children 
learn from their parents, and is absolutely necessary for driving. One should always be 
able to repair their own car. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's 
lawful owner, from tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans 
should have an unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Please consider the importance of a competent society, and not one reliant on private 
corporations for repair and function. It is the responsibility of every responsible 
American to learn to be independent and be able to repair/improve the devices we 
legally purchase. Corporations feel the need to nickel-and-dime individuals with 
unnecessary newer devices when older ones fail - many of these failures can be fixed, 
putting money back into the pockets of individuals who will in turn spend their money in 
other ways. It is important that the marketplace recognize competence and innovation - 
and having the freedom to edit and improve the devices we own is an essential part of 
that. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers - we are the future rights holders, and the think tanks of much greater 
innovation. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

The thing is that the DMCA legislation was passed at a time when many emerging 
technologies were new to market and those market forces and legislators did not 
understand the full impact those technologies and legislation would have. Now, it has 
been years that have since seen a radical and marked change in not only technology, 
but the way it is integrated into our society and further how we interact with it. Back in 
times gone past, if you wanted to get under the hood of your car to make whatever 
modifications you wanted, you were able to do so. If you wanted to replace a stock part 
for something from a different maker, you weren't violating any laws - you bought the 
car, therefore, whatever changes you deemed necessary or simply wanted to make, 
you made. I believe that code in the ECUs falls under a similar category; that although 
the code itself my be proprietary, if you reverse-engineered and recoded that very 
same code would it not be brand new code? Just as new ages and new technology 
emerge, so do new laws and legislation to cover what has been happening and what 
will continue to happen in the future. Hampering our rights not only as consumers, but 
as Americans, in a country that was built and thrives upon freedom, will only prove 
detrimental to innovation in the future and a point of contention in the present. Please 
have the presence of mind to allow us to keep our rights, not just as consumers, but as 
Americans.

I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Brendan O'Bryant. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles.

abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Bryce Nash. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles.Ú
Ú
I purchased and race a 2014 model year electric car. This electric vehicle has the latest 
state of the art systems for vehicle controls, which means that several systems are 
highly integrated. In order to compete with this vehicle, modifications are necessary to 
allow it to perform in a manner which gets it around a race course faster, an accepted 
reality in the century-old practice of improving automotive technology on the test bed of 
racing. These modifications pose no harm to the original manufacturer, and if anything 
could serve to enhance automotive technology for all. Ú
Ú
Future modifications to automotive systems regarding safety and security mechanisms 
must also be considered. Automotive OEMs are not required to use any standardized 
diagnostic and repair information for airbag, braking, tire pressure monitoring, stability 
control, etc. systems. As these vehicles age, any repairs must be done at dealership 
due to the proprietary nature of these systems. Unfortunately, this is extremely 
expensive compared to the value of older vehicles, which means owners will either be 
forced to drive unsafe vehicles or scrap otherwise fine vehicles because cheaper repair 
methods are unavailable on the open market. Clearly, repairing the safety systems on 
your own vehicle should not be a crime, which is why a standardized on board 
diagnostic protocol exists for engines. Without such a standard for safety systems, 
[PAGE 357]
owners should be free to modify their car to keep it performing safely as necessary.  
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles.Ú
Ú
I come from a farm family.  Prompt, affordable repairs of essential equipment can make 
the difference between crops harvested and crops spoiling in the field with a 
subsequently bankrupt farm.  When repairs can be made simply in the field, farmers do 
that.  But when the software in the engine's computer requires branded parts and 
access by password possessing authorized repairmen, the repairs aren't made in the 
field and are neither prompt nor often affordable.  Give the farmer who owns the tractor, 
the engine, the pistons, and the plow access to the software so that the crops can be 
brought in before they spoil. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

intentioned people from using their electronics as they see fit is doing nothing to fight 
piracy. A pirate does not care if it's legal to do this or that. What a pirate does will still 
remain illegal, and they still won't care. Leaving these restrictions in place does not 
somehow make piracy "illegal-er."

I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Christine McCracken. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms-- not to mention making the rich richer! I should have the right to remix, 
modify, and repair the things that I own. As electronics are integrated into every kind of 
product, please consider the needs of consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, David Dobrowski. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

preventing others from being able to copy their design or work and claim it as their own. 
In other words, Apple is the only company that can produce and claim as their own the 
iPad. Who should own an individual iPad? The purchaser to do with as he pleases: to 
use, to break, to add and remove software from, to sell to another person. But the 
purchaser should be limited in that he cannot sell that iPad while claiming it for their 
own work as something other than an iPad made by Apple. Just as a book cannot be 
published without the express permission of the author but the books that are 
purchased are owned by the purchaser to do with as they please. If the purchaser of a 
book desires to burn the book, they may. If they wish to sell the book to another 
person, they may. If the purchaser wishes to remove some pages from the book they 
may. So hardware, physical objects, should have the same ownership but not the rights 
to distribute as one's own intellectual work. Nor the right to copy significant portions of 
the book and distribute it free or paid without an agreement with the original author. 
 
Copyright it's being abused to take ownership away from purchasers and pass it to the 
owners of the intellectual property. Copyright law is twisted to stifle creativity, limit 
consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital freedoms. I 
[PAGE 579]
should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As electronics 
are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of consumers as 
well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

I'm a member of a small slice of Americans: I fix things instead of throwing them out 
when they break.  As an example, I have a Volkswagen that is old enough to vote.Ú
Ú
There are opportunities to modify the electronic parameters in the engine control unit 
(ECU) to change the car's performance and fuel economy to better suit my needs.  The 
ECU in the car contains a software map that takes as input things like throttle position, 
car speed, and air temperature and determines how much fuel to inject into each 
piston.  I cannot legally change this program, even though I own this car.  Every single 
bit of it is owned by me and can be resold by me to another person, but incongruously I 
am prohibited from changing the code on the computer within the engine compartment.Ú
Ú
Please change the law to make this legal. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. It was intended to 
provide an absolute monopoly for the author *for a limited time*.  But it's being abused 
to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle creativity, 
limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital freedoms. 
I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As electronics 
are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of consumers as 
well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Duke Briscoe. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Emily Dirsh. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
There should be a distinction between the rights of owners of motorized land vehicles 
to repair and customize their purchases, without being in violation of Copyright Law.  
Without the ability to control the use of owned assets - the buyer is no longer a buyer 
but an unwilling, and often unwitting, licensee.  
 
Copyright claims that intrude on the owners' use of purchased equipment are unfair to 
owners.  
Thank you for your consideration.

Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Glenn Madere. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of

Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Jack Dubnicek. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

[PAGE 979]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, James Sneeringer. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Strong copyright protections are essential to the U.S. economy. If companies are 
allowed to distribute copyrighted content they did not produce, it could seriously harm 
incentives to invest in high quality content and software production. 
 
However, copyright law must not be allowed to abuse individual end users, and prevent 
their full use of property they own. Firmware can only run on the device for which it is 
specifically written; there is little fear of any harm from piracy of firmware. To run it you 
need the right device, for which the manufacturer was paid in the first sale. 
 
If a person owns a device they should have full legal access to it firmware. Otherwise 
property rights will be hollowed out from within.

going to cut it with our growing needs in this world. An exemption doesn't need to be 
made but it must be made and if it doesn't happen now, believe me it will happen soon 
eventually when our world population and food crisis will not be able to wait 4 days for 
their diminishing supplies. I hope you take this into consideration and give a farmer

I am providing comments on behalf of myself, jason howard. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

[PAGE 1043]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Jeffrey Justice. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
As a member of the lower middle class and a working American with little to spare, 
repairing my vehicle is both a hobby and and a budgeting tool. My vehicles are at least 
ten years old, but when the time comes to purchase a new vehicle, I am the lawful 
owner of the vehicle, and unless my repair efforts can be proven to be attempts at 
circumventing the manufacturer's safeguards in order to illegally profit from the results, 
I shall remain forever more, a peaceful member of society, engaged in the age-old 
practice of working with my hands.  
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. Wilbur and Orville 
Wright attempted to secure the intellectual rights to their invention by means of the U.S. 
Patent Office shortly after their successful aviation experiments in 1903, and yet rivals 
continued to hound the brothers well after Wilbur's death in efforts to discredit the 
Wrights as the true inventors of the airplane. 
It was the patents that secured the invention in the early days, but it was the Wright's 
persistent lawsuits that kept the hounds at bay. And yet today, the ability to build an 
airplane is shared across the world and the credit, rightly earned by Wilbur and Orville 
Wright is attributed without the need for copyright infringement lawsuits every time a 
company wants to build an airplane. The respect for the original inventions has fallen 
into a sort of public domain, and earning the right to fly is a humanistic goal, now that 
the aerodynamic tables created by the Wright's wind tunnel experiments are proven 
every time a jet liner takes flight. 
  It is no small thing to acknowledge that every experiment carries some potential, 
whether intended and understood or not. Let the freedom of innovation know only the 
borders embroiled by a wing as it lifts a hundred human beings into the air. Let no fear 
accompany the right to repair what one person has acquired for themselves. Let those 
[PAGE 1044]
who create valuable software be properly compensated for their work, and also let the 
limits of their intellectual ownership be clearly defined so that consumers are aware of 
the limitations of the software licenses they purchase. 
 
And let us work with compassion and dignity towards each other to create a solution to 
this immense and pivotal issue. Let our grandchildren be able to use Grandfather's tool 
set and Grandmother's Javascript debugger. We owe our children the freedom to 
repair, and be repaired.  
 
Thank you for your time 
 
Jeffrey R. Justice

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor

embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from

[PAGE 1153]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, John Galley. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

I am providing comments on behalf of myself, John Simmons. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

[PAGE 1183]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, John Waiveris. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
I am a software developer and repair my own cars.  However, I increasingly am 
concerned that new cars are not repairable without highly specialized tools, secret 
APIs, and secret encryption keys.  For example, my 1996 Ford Ranger needed a 
$3000 electrical tool to bleed the ABS brakes.  As an older car, the tool was no longer 
available and the local Ford dealer no longer had the tool.  Luckily, there I found an 
online discussion about mechanical trick that saved me from having to remove the 
entire ABS system just to keep the car.  Ú
Ú
Though this is just the beginning.  Newer cars are taking this same process to a new 
level.  The tools are even more expensive and there are no mechanical trick that can 
get around encryption.  Even worse, by making these tools copyrighted, even 
discussing or building tools to fix my car can result in a lawsuit.  Ú
Ú
Obviously market forces aren't preventing manufacturers from building cars without 
these digital locks.  Please add a DMCA exemption to enable a healthy market in which 
people can maintain their own cars. 
 
undefined

could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Farmers grow the food you eat everyday.  Restricting farmers to rely on unchangeable, 
locked systems only repairable by manufacturers limits the production potential of 
agricultural producers everywhere.  This translates to an immeasurable decrease in the 
food supply chain just from delayed work times.  Taking away the ability to repair, 
maintain, and possibly improve a producer's equipment goes against every notion that 
a farmer's ingenuity is unmatched in our society.  Making this illegal challenges the 
roots this country was built on.  The farmer finds ways to "make hay when the sun 
shines" however he/she has to, but they shouldn't have to break the law to do it.  
Please, let those who feed the world do what they've been doing best for generations, 
growing the most and the best food possible in the most optimal conditions made 
available to them.  Thank you.Ú

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Kenneth Kolbly. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright law, along with Patent law, was originally designed to encourage creativity 
and fuel innovation. And it has succeeded at that.  But copyright, and specifically the 
DMCA, is currently being abused by content owners to do exactly the opposite. Every 
single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle 
property rights, and chip away at our digital freedoms. This is a property rights and/or 
fair use issue. Most of the best engineers in this country started out as youngsters by 
taking apart the things that they (or their parents) owned and learning to understand 
them. To continue to support the development of these top-notch inventors and 
engineers, it is imperative that modification and tinkering is permitted from the lowest 
levels.   It is essential that all of us have the legal right to modify and repair the things 
that we own.  I can legally take a printed book and cut it up for a display or copy 
passages to post on my wall.  This right to fair use must extend to all copyrighted 
content.  The type or location of the content should not exempt it.    Electronics are 
being integrated into every kind of product and copyright is being used to protect the 
software in those devices, making this issue pervasive in every walk of life.  Please 
consider the needs of consumers as well as those of the rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Kim MacCartney. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Kyle Lutter. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Matthew Footer. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
When my Chevy Nova needed a new radiator I didn't have to get permission from 
Chevy to replace it. When my Buick Skylark needed a carb rebuild I just did it, without 
needing to get an unlock code from Buick. When my Honda Civic needed new drive 
axels I just bought some rebuilt sand tossed them in, same goes for the timing belt. 
When I wanted better sound I simply ripped out the original head unit and put in my 
own. The idea that car owners don't own the code running through their car is 
ludicrous.  If some car manufacturer wants to retain possession of part of my car then 
they can pay for repairs.  
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Michael Chung. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the

vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from

unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
As far as I understand it, the ostensible purpose of copyright is to fuel creativity and 
innovation by giving people a financial incentive to create and innovate.  Copyright is 
now being abused to do exactly the opposite.  Creativity and innovation do no happen 
in a vacuum, they build on things that came before.  One of the major groups of people 
who innovate, benefiting us all, are people who like to tinker (think Apple and 
Microsoft).  When copyright law prevents people from understanding the products they 
buy and own, and from improving upon then, copyright then stifles innovation and 
encourages rent-seeking, not innovation: 
 
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rent-seeking 
 
Copyright has a place, but it's reach and abuse has crossed a line where innovation 
and creativity are hindered.  Please allow Americans to continue be a culture of tinkers 
and innovators! 
 
Sincerely, 
 
Nathan
