Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Noah Davis. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from

unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles.

freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Richard Small. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

[PAGE 1835]
Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Rich West. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
As the owner of several classic cars, I gain great enjoyment out of the creativity one 
can apply to  the stock manufacturer platform which is provided as a base to work 
from.  As an IT professional, that creative outlet is enhanced by the additional features 
on modern vehicles.  Personal customization of the vehicle, regardless of its age, must 
continue unhindered in order to spur progress: how many new unique designs have 
come from those that tinker in their own garage?  Current law prohibits any person, 
including the vehicle's lawful owner, from tampering with the electronic "locks", at any 
time, auto manufacturers have put into place to guard the computer systems that are 
installed in modern vehicles. That's silly. Americans should have an unfettered right to 
repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to protect, for a short time, fresh new ideas from the thievery 
of others hoping to cash in on the profits.  The intention was to encourage creativity 
and fuel innovation while allowing a short time to protect those ideas. Yet as each 
minute ticks onwards, the intention of the law is being forgotten and the law itself is  
being abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to 
stifle creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our 
digital freedoms. As a free consumer in the United States, ownership should not come 
with strings attached: I should have the right to modify and repair the things that I own 
regardless of the format they are in; be it analog or digital. As electronics are integrated 
into every kind of product, please consider the needs of consumers as well as rights 
holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Russell Riall. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being

consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
I should have the right to archive any digital media I legally purchase for my own 
private use. I should have the right to translate any digital media I have purchased for 
my own private use from one digital format to another, possibly more advanced, digital 
format in order to preserve my ability to use that media. Copyright laws are meant to be 
used to protect the rights of the author and should not be used as a way to obsolesce 
content. How many times will everyone have to buy the "White Album" again?

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Steven boykin. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

right for the provider of their choice to repair or modify their own vehicle, if they so 
choose, and not be limited to the options provided by the manufacturer.  
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Victor Palma. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, William Alton. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor

abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.

Short Comment Regarding a Proposed 
Exemption 
Under 17 U.S.C. 1201 
 
Item 1. Commenter Information 
 
I am providing comments on behalf of myself, Zach Johnson. 
 
Item 2. Proposed Class Addressed 
 
Proposed Class 21: Vehicle software – diagnosis, repair, or modification 
 
Item 3. Statement Regarding Proposed Exemption 
 
Most people would never suspect that repairing or tinkering with their own car or tractor 
could be illegal. These days, though, many manufacturers now put digital locks on the 
embedded software that operates our increasingly sophisticated, computer-controlled 
vehicles. Current law prohibits any person, including the vehicle's lawful owner, from 
tampering with those locks for any purpose. That's silly. Americans should have an 
unfettered right to repair and modify their own vehicles. 
 
Copyright was designed to encourage creativity and fuel innovation. But it's being 
abused to do exactly the opposite. Every single day, copyright law is twisted to stifle 
creativity, limit consumer choice, dismantle property rights, and chip away at our digital 
freedoms. I should have the right to remix, modify, and repair the things that I own. As 
electronics are integrated into every kind of product, please consider the needs of 
consumers as well as rights holders. 
 
Thank you for your consideration.
